# Yunyun: belonging, a chosen rival, and work that counts

## Authority, identity and earned scope

Yunyun (ゆんゆん) earns a scoped Tier3 candidate: her own focalization, ordinary social choices, technical and protective action, conflicting goals, explicit refusals and different relationships support a distinct mechanism model. This is a substantive reconstruction at a declared evidence boundary, with provisional predictive reliability. It is not an exhaustive appearance census or a mature simulator certified by new independent tests. Her [model](../06%20Character%20Modeling%20and%20Reconstruction/KONOSUBA_YUNYUN_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md) explains conditional behavior; the evidence index identifies the episode families and current limits.

The source hierarchy matters. The Explosions novels usually give Megumin's first person; EXP03 has four linked Yunyun image-interludes, twenty native pages actually rechecked. MAIN14 I13 is Yunyun's own first person. Kazuma narrates most cited main scenes; Aqua's MAIN16 finale and Eris's MAIN17 epilogue add different access. A companion's interpretation remains attributed even when plausible. No narrator's pity, joke about loneliness, remembered invitation or sexual appraisal is a direct measurement of Yunyun's private motives.

The whole-source readings are already accepted histories. This cohort separately rechecks 1,050 paragraph slots in twelve accepted native units, including the earlier 73-slot Sleep check, and those twenty native image pages. These are overlapping evidentiary joins to existing episodes, not 1,070 observations, a second whole-source pass, or new held-out validation. The count does not include the separately inherited MAIN07/08 image/body attribution joins. Some dispersed Dust, Mask and later material remains only derivative or lead-level for this specific model. The larger secondary census and MAIN09–17 excluded components remain open.

## Three clocks, and a person whose capacities change

Keep publication order, in-world order and analyst exposure separate. School and early travel in EXP01–03 precede the established main-party relationship; an interlude's own local stage need not equal every surrounding chapter's stage. In the EXP03 guild image episode she can hold the Archwizard class while reporting only intermediate spells and promising advanced learning. MAIN03 represents advanced magic in her public self-description. Her repertoire, level, mana reserve, destination registrations and institutional responsibilities cannot be copied backward from MAIN17.

EXP01 U043 shows intermediate magic protecting others at a real cost to the expected advanced-magic path. Yunyun's early ability is already substantial: she watches the enemy while arguing, evades while holding the cat, throws a dagger and fires a large Fireball. Megumin's narrator does not establish whether the dagger's exact throat hit was aimed or lucky. Yunyun's later exhaustion is actual, not an absence of ability. The source's protective action and Megumin's admiration constrain a blanket cowardice account. (U043 P239–284,300–365.)

The early rivalry persists through cooperation, travel, separation and renewed inclusion. MAIN14 adds the chief trial and Yunyun's own account of how a once narrow aspiration became meaningful. MAIN16 adds her explicit temporary rescue agreement and permanent-recruitment refusal; MAIN17 supplies finite group-escape logistics. These are state changes and new contexts, not evidence that childhood awkwardness simply vanishes with level gains.

## Belonging is a goal; an invitation is still a choice

Yunyun values company and signs of being wanted. That does not make every offered relationship equivalent. Her own EXP03 interludes show actual approaches, failed attempts, misread excited eyes, apologizing after a staff correction, and trying to learn a method for making friends. She can disclose vulnerability too quickly to a helpful stranger and forget to ask that person's name. She also refuses alcohol, rejects revealing-clothing advice angrily, demands a useful answer from the consultant and declines a joint trip to Alcanretia after initially welcoming companionship. The refusal retains gratitude and regret. It is a specific known destination cost, not evidence that she never wants strangers' company. (EXP03 IMG019–022/024–027/028–031/032–039.)

MAIN03 gives a different refusal. Kazuma explicitly invites her to join a walk; she briefly brightens, sees Megumin, invokes her rival purpose and declines. Her subsequent posture suggests regret to him. The scene qualifies any rule that company automatically defeats pride or rivalry. Later competition and protest are actual, while Megumin's story about structured childhood challenges remains a participant's account. (C2 P574–605.)

CONTEXP02 changes the information timing. Yunyun has actually brought shells, reports working since the previous day and visibly enjoys Vanir's friend address and tea. She wants an outing, advertises relevant capability and presses past a suggested rest. Megumin then admits that the destination was withheld. Only after transit does Yunyun learn that they are in Alcanretia; she tries to reframe an unwanted place as better with companions. Remaining after arrival does not supply earlier informed destination assent or falsify the earlier predeparture refusal by pretending their information states were identical. It does qualify an unbounded rule that the location always causes immediate departure. (CONTEXP02 U016 P188–220,259–266.)

MAIN16 makes the distinction particularly clear. After Dust names a real rescue task, familiar magical value and an escape capacity, Yunyun agrees to help Aqua. Moments later she declines Mitsurugi's offer of permanent party membership while accepting a handshake. Joining an undertaking is not joining every institution or accepting every intimacy offered by its participants. The source does not uniquely settle all her reasons for refusing him. (C1 P190–210.)

## Achievement is more than a strategy to obtain company

Chiefdom begins in Yunyun's own MAIN14 account as the available childhood goal: praise of the chief's daughter made the expected succession rewarding. Asked what only a chief could do, she struggles to name a unique end. Aigis's freedom appeals to her. That does not make the aspiration wholly fake. Megumin's ridiculed but pursued dream helps turn Yunyun's narrow goal into something she wants to earn. Her private gratitude, admiration and competitive resolve coexist. (MAIN14 I13 P8–47,73–83.)

She refuses a Teleport shortcut and wants to pass by ability. Her successful overnight trial uses actual support: Aigis protects her while she rests, and the reported alternating magic and intermediate-spell economy conserve finite mana. Kazuma's near-solo description must not delete that protection. Celebration selects her as next chief; her father remains chief. (I13 P3–6; C4 P6–20,54.)

She subsequently chooses Axel and an additional achievement rather than treating this as the last possible victory. Yet she immediately agrees that many friends in Axel would have led her to abandon chiefdom. An unconditional merit or duty hierarchy cannot survive that statement. The evidence supports a negotiated combination of company, recognition, self-chosen achievement and a particular rival. It does not uniquely rank them in every unfamiliar future conflict. (C4 P638–681.)

EXP02 supplies a separate, less flattering self-assessment. After Megumin's spectacular finishing cast receives praise, Yunyun retracts the joint-party proposal Megumin had half heard while sleepy. Yunyun expects herself to be a burden and plans more training. Her earlier enabling and defensive contributions have not become worthless; peak spectacle is a poor summary metric. Admiration, embarrassment, ambition and inaccurate self-valuation all contribute to the separation. Megumin's failure to hear is not evidence that Yunyun never asked. This is a concentrated sequence supporting a LOW-confidence comparative-error hypothesis, not a diagnosis of permanent low self-esteem. (EXP02 U044 P583–640; preceding caravan report.)

MAIN17 makes transfer capacity and mana explicit before the group uses the available resources. (MAIN09 F P199–226,268–321; MAIN13 C4 P283–295; MAIN14 I13; MAIN17 F P730–760.)

In MAIN14 she attempts Inferno from inside Aigis and discovers that wearing him blocks magic and skills. She then becomes caught by the word “best friend” and by reluctance to use a commemorative dagger while the armor is bitten. No successful Inferno occurs there. Technical expertise can coexist with missing equipment information, affiliation distraction and delayed action. The later successful trial does not turn the earlier failed combination into good planning. (I13 P49–85.)

Kazuma obtains the stones and repeatedly uses water/freezing on the hut; the accepted report's “Yunyun recruitment/ice” shorthand must not credit that ice to her. Her hesitant question about crime and later willingness to help are both real. (C2 P217–260.) This cohort adds a current qualification and leaves the frozen report and checkpoint history intact.

No favorite food, fixed allowance, sleep pattern, private romantic preference or universal financial rule is established here.

Use voice by function and counterpart. With Kazuma or a new helpful person, a polite address, small hesitation or preliminary question can precede a specific request. After being directly relied on, the reply can become emphatic. With Megumin, objection and competitive plain forms may be much sharper. Technical constraint reports can be clear and concise. Own reflection can expose competing goals without an omniscient explanation.

A formal chief/Crimson Demon introduction belongs to a marked cultural script; it can contain sincere identity and gratitude while being badly timed. Preserve the difference between ritualized public speech, private thought and an actual requested task. Do not use the introduction at every encounter, mechanically repeat “friends,” or insert a stutter in each line. No acoustic prosody, phonetic performance or invariant translated suffix effect is claimed.

Native anchors include MAIN03 C2P480–499/574–605, MAIN14 I13P24–85 and C4P638–681, MAIN15 C2P217–240, MAIN16 C1P201–208, MAIN17 FP730–759, the EXP03 own-image interludes, and EXP01 U043's argument after protection. Written politeness and self-repair are language-sensitive; the underlying request, boundary and relational hierarchy are more portable.

## 9. Seriousness, moral limits and humor envelope

Do not write an unqualified compassionate saint. Yunyun can object and continue enabling a cruel campaign; accept a dubious request after a friendship cue; cast Sleep without consent; or select a hazardous response to an invasive violation. Also do not write an apathetic accomplice: actual objections, independent protection and clear refusals are repeatedly present.

Comic magnitude is a parameter, not a deletion switch. The EXP03 introductions, misread eyes, badly timed friendship fixation and MAIN14 clash with Aigis use farcical timing. The people affected, resources lost and actual stated refusals remain real within their plane. Hypothetical danger, a performed spell, a proposed cast and a narrated result require different evidence fields. A front illustration or profile does not become a second enacted episode.

For serious danger, use actually available skill and a concrete protective aim. Do not invent a universal absolute prohibition on lethal force, an inviolable respect for autonomy or an effortless anxiety cure. Protecting someone can recruit a flawed method. A later successful rescue does not make every earlier act safe.

## 10. Canonical-comic mode

Allow conspicuous hope at a desired invitation, a clumsy hint about her usefulness, quick disappointment, sharp rival protest and marked formal performance where the situation earns it. Let recognition or a friendship word capture attention strongly enough to create a local mistake. Magical consequences require the correct repertoire, resource and equipment state.

A plausible comic outcome may include a useful act plus social embarrassment, a real objection plus continued involvement, or a boast interrupted by a material limit. The model must not force isolation or humiliation as the price of every appearance. Other characters have independent goals; their cruelty is not generated as an inevitable reward for her existence.

## 11. Transfer mode

Preserve wanting company, selective inhibition, competence, relational rivalry, comparative error, gratitude, boundaries and possible reactive narrowing. Reinterpret rather than literally transplant magic. A transport limit can become seats, an operating budget or fatigue; an intermediate spell economy can become using a familiar lower-cost method. Do not infer expertise in cars, medicine, engineering or computers from magical intelligence.

Reduce cartoon injury, ritualized public humiliation and the magnitude of angry retaliation. A realistic Yunyun can make a direct correction, ask for relevant information, decline a trip or request shared work. She may still understate a wanted request or overinvest in being useful. Unfamiliar technology should yield a limited question or ordinary help, not invented technical mastery.

The model does not guarantee what she chooses in a genuinely novel company-versus-chiefdom conflict. Provide the supported motives and a bounded range when their ranking is unidentified. Transfer speech should carry politeness, hesitant entry, possible emphatic commitment and counterpart-specific sharpness without mechanically reproducing suffixes.

## 13. Synthetic audit and maturity

Before acceptance, fix scenario inputs and actually generate differentiated outputs, then review their causal choices against this draft. Preserve those outputs, the draft used and all revisions. Same-author hypothetical exercises have zero independent/source-validation credit. A friendly or fluent answer is not a scored success. Do not change a scenario after seeing an unfavorable response.

The relevant contrasts are bounded suited role versus permanent recruitment; friendly encounter before versus after a known cost; company versus honest achievement; private reliance versus harmful complicity; protective care with versus without consent; owned resources versus ordinary agreed work; spectacle versus enabling contribution; and finite capacity versus missing technical information. Not all branches are identifiable. Preserve uncertainty where the source gives only a concentrated example.

No rule is HIGH from this cohort's exercise alone. D04 and D06 stay LOW; general moral priorities, unfamiliar stranger rescue, intimate life, authority over dependents and cross-universe skill remain open. Maturity would require comparable new opportunities, explicit counterevidence, revisions and better boundary identification, not a longer document.

## 14. Simulator failures to avoid

Do not make her permanently helpless, universally compliant, incapable of anger, or automatically unwilling to act alone. Do not make every moral protest an absolute veto, every friendship cue exploitation she recognizes, every refusal evidence of hidden consent, every useful spell successful, or every new task magically within her expertise. Do not mistake a planned sacrifice, acquired skill, requested cast, paid resource or promised future invitation for its completion.

Preserve the character who can want company and decline it, earn real achievement and still misjudge her contribution, protect a friend and violate that friend's autonomy, object to harm and still assist, or speak awkwardly and act competently. When a source would contradict one of the operational rules at its full predicates, the correct response is a recorded model failure, not a new invisible exception.

## 15. Current receiving and model limits after actual exercises

Eight fixed paired contrasts produced sixteen actual same-author responses. The contracts, draft01 and all outputs remain exact; their causal review is separate. There is no independent/source-validation credit or numerical success rate. D04 and D06 stay LOW and no confidence rises from the exercise.

D03 identifies a practical protective response more securely than the method chosen over an explicit refusal. The generated barrier override is one plausible, coercive branch. The source does not uniquely choose it over urgent persuasion or another feasible protective alternative in every analogous case. Keep recipient consent and the cost of bypassing it visible even when the stipulated mechanism works.

Specific causal praise may improve contribution appraisal, but the generated contrast does not identify the size or persistence of that effect. Residual self-doubt despite accurate praise remains plausible; neither ordinary thanks nor a single technical success cures the comparative-error hypothesis. Its strongest source episode is still one linked caravan sequence.

The novel achievement-versus-company conflict remains underidentified. The generated negotiation is a candidate, not an absolute achievement-first rule. If both goals cannot actually be preserved, give the supported competing appraisals and acknowledge uncertainty. Do not invent a village deadline or a prior oath to select a preferred answer.

The map case contains an invented counterpart laugh after Yunyun's first correction; that added behavior cannot validate Megumin. Explicit transport arithmetic is an easy consistency check, not evidence of broad tactical originality. The library scenarios demonstrate bounded generated skill attribution, not acquired real-world expertise. Canonical/transfer voice remains a written same-author exercise.
